newsitem.title: HONG KONG: CITIC shrs down further on placement fear.
newsitem.headline: CITIC shrs down further on placement fear.

text.p: Shares of conglomerate CITIC Pacific Ltd, the second-most actively trade stock by turnover on Tuesday, fell further in late afternoon trade on worries of a possible placement of shares in the future, brokers said.
"Investors were continuously taking profit on concern of a possible placement of shares in the future," said Anthony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas.
CITIC Pacific, which fell HK$2.40 or 5.63 percent on Monday, eased a further HK$0.90 or 2.24 percent to HK$39.30 in late trade. Volume was 23.10 million shares worth HK$912.18 million.
Analysts said the market was worried that CITIC Pacific management might place out shares after they take a 15.47 percent stake from the company's parent at HK$33 per share.
"The deal can suggest less support from the parent in future which can affect its earnings in the long run, and that is seen giving investors an excuse to take profit," one broker said.

Last week, CITIC said its management team headed by chairman Larry Yung would buy a 15.47 percent stake in the company at HK$33 per share from parent China International Trust & Investment Corp Hong Kong (Holdings) Ltd.
